! Check now (nothing rolls this back by itself):

!   In the second terminal:   open a NEW ssh session to dev-cisco-same-address-block as yourself, then: terminal length 0, show privilege (must say 15)
! When both checks are fine, type this one command yourself:  write memory
! To undo: tacctl device config plan dev-cisco-same-address-block --backout (tacctl keeps this
! plan's back-out: after the check pull has replaced the picture, the command still prints this
! plan's, and says which pull it undoes, until the next plan with changes)
! Do not: 'write memory' before the check; paste outside the banners; paste into another device;
! paste on a console more than twenty lines at a time; keep this output in a file after the paste
! Locked out (the paste cut your session and no login works)? A superuser runs: tacctl breakglass hold dev-cisco-same-address-block --reason "..."

! fix or back out, and the superuser runs: tacctl breakglass release dev-cisco-same-address-block

warnings: the server entry tacacs server OLD-TACACS is at the address of the standard server, and IOS refuses a second entry with the same address and key: the region removes it (and the group entries that name it) before it adds the standard block, and the back-out puts it back; command authorization is taken off first and typed again last, while the server still answers

the block switches command authorization on ('aaa authorization commands', 'config-commands') with its last lines: from then on every command is authorized by the server, so paste it as a user the server knows (or with local first), and keep the second terminal for the back-out
cleanup_deferred: cleanup comes after this region is pasted and verified: pull the device, then plan --converge again
